Its English page uses small business broadly in this place-of-supply discussion. Do not read that wording as a test applying only below a small-business turnover threshold. The actual purchasing purpose and supply are the relevant starting facts here.

sections.heading: Find the establishment that receives the service
paragraphs: For business services within the general rule, the receiving fixed establishment governs; otherwise the buyer’s business establishment does. Vero looks at the personnel and technical resources used to receive the service. A VAT number alone does not establish those facts.

If the group adds American staff or premises, review the actual arrangement. Also keep the VAT fixed-establishment question distinct from the separate income-tax treaty test; similar terminology does not make them the same legal decision.

sections.heading: Retain the Finnish reporting result and check exceptions
paragraphs: Vero says certain non-Finnish service sales, including general-rule sales to non-EU countries, are reported under Turnover taxable at zero VAT rate. That return label should not cause the team to omit a qualifying foreign service sale from the return.

The EU recapitulative-statement discussion concerns qualifying sales into other EU countries. Do not copy it to an American customer or assume an EU reverse-charge system there. Vero directs the seller to investigate the destination’s tax treatment. Property services, admission, catering and other named services have special rules; installed goods and construction also need their own classification.

sections.heading: Fictional example: support and equipment installation
paragraphs: A Helsinki brand offers remote operating support and a separate equipment installation at an American site. The finance manager asks which establishment receives the support and documents its business use. She then separates the equipment and installation rather than using one international-services account to establish both treatments.

The resulting file explains each invoice decision and the supported Finnish return entry, while assigning the American tax questions to a separate reviewer. If facts about foreign staff or premises remain uncertain, the team records them and considers the appropriate request for written guidance or an advance ruling. This example organises questions; it does not decide the installation’s treatment.

sections.heading: Prepare a record the finance team can use
bullets: Buyer identity, business purpose and actual receiving-establishment resources.
A breakdown of support, goods, installation and any special-rule services.
Invoice decision and the supported Finnish return entry.
Foreign staff/premises facts, destination-tax questions and any request for official written guidance.

practicalOutput: A buyer, establishment and supply record supporting each invoice and Finnish VAT-return decision, with U.S. tax questions assigned separately.
limitations: This is a narrow home-country VAT guide, not a full corporate-income-tax, withholding, transfer-pricing, foreign-exchange or U.S. tax analysis.
Service type, business/private use, receiving establishment, physical location and any special rule must be established. A U.S. address or incorporation certificate alone does not approve the result.
Franchise classification, state sales rules, staffing permissions, U.S. work authorization, data transfers and local operating requirements remain independent research tasks.
learningSummary: A Finnish company may supply ordinary support to an American customer and also deliver goods or installation work. Before choosing value added tax (VAT) treatment, the team must identify each supply, the customer’s business use and the establishment receiving it; a foreign invoice can still require Finnish reporting.

keyTerms.meaning: Value added tax; the Finnish invoice and reporting question is separate from American taxes.
A relevant business presence assessed through the personnel and technical resources receiving the service, not just a registration number.
The country treated as the service’s location for the relevant VAT rule.
The separate EU reporting mechanism described for qualifying sales to other EU countries.

title: Austrian invoices for U.S. services: prove the customer and identify each service
description: Explain the Austrian customer-location rule without applying EU reporting routines automatically to America.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Establish the customer and place before choosing the invoice treatment
paragraphs: Section 3a(6) of the Austrian VAT Act generally follows the business customer’s place of business, or the establishment receiving the service, subject to the stated exceptions. The reviewed current version is effective January 1, 2025. The Ministry of Finance’s January 2026 guidance separately identifies property, transport, event-admission and other services needing special attention.
Begin with the actual contracting entity, purchasing purpose and service. Payment in dollars or an American incorporation document does not identify every receiving-establishment or exception fact.

sections.heading: Ask for appropriate American business evidence
paragraphs: The Austrian Federal Economic Chamber, WKO, distinguishes an EU VAT-number check from the documents used to prove that a third-country customer is a business. It gives an appropriate tax-administration certificate as an example. Do not leave the analysis unresolved simply because the American buyer cannot provide an EU VAT identifier.

Business documents are not decisive if the purchase is exclusively for private purposes: the guidance treats that buyer as a private customer. If private use is uncertain, ask and document the actual purpose rather than treating a business name as the answer.

sections.heading: Keep EU reporting and American taxes separate
paragraphs: The Ministry’s recapitulative-statement discussion concerns qualifying services placed in another EU Member State. WKO directs third-country transactions to the destination’s own tax rules. Establish the Austrian place-of-supply and invoice result, check the applicable Austrian reporting, and assign the American tax questions separately.

This guide does not establish an American VAT reverse charge, an Austrian filing exemption for every export or the complete treatment of a bundled service. The cited primary rule and guidance were interpreted with AI assistance; the full set of statutory exceptions and implementing regulations was not surveyed.

sections.heading: Fictional example: Vienna support plus admission to a local workshop
paragraphs: A Vienna company supplies management support to an American business and charges for attendance at a workshop in Austria. The controller obtains evidence of the actual buyer and its business purpose. She identifies which establishment receives the support, then asks how the workshop is supplied and whether an admission or other exception applies.

One customer paying both invoices does not make the supplies identical. The team records separate reasons for the chosen treatment and identifies any remaining factual question before issuing the invoices. This protects the accounting decision from relying on a billing address alone; it does not decide the workshop’s actual tax result.

sections.heading: Assemble the invoice decision file
bullets: Appropriate third-country business-status evidence and the actual purchasing purpose.
Contracting entity and receiving establishment for each service.
A breakdown of support, property work, admission and other relevant components.
The Austrian invoice decision, reporting check and unresolved exceptions.
A named person to investigate U.S. taxes and the separate operating, personnel and relationship questions.

practicalOutput: A documented customer, receiving-establishment and service breakdown supporting Austrian invoicing and reporting, with U.S. taxes assigned separately.
limitations: This is a narrow home-country VAT guide, not a full corporate-income-tax, withholding, transfer-pricing, foreign-exchange or U.S. tax analysis.
Service type, business/private use, receiving establishment, physical location and any special rule must be established. A U.S. address or incorporation certificate alone does not approve the result.
Franchise classification, state sales rules, staffing permissions, U.S. work authorization, data transfers and local operating requirements remain independent research tasks.
German source text was interpreted with AI assistance. Only the cited primary-rule scope is established; the full range of statutory exceptions and implementing regulations is not surveyed.
learningSummary: An Austrian supplier needs to establish who buys a service and which establishment receives it before deciding its value added tax (VAT) treatment. An American buyer may provide different business evidence from an EU customer, and a package including an Austrian workshop may need more than one service decision.

keyTerms.meaning: Value added tax; this guide addresses the Austrian side of the invoice.
A customer outside the European Union; here the proposed buyer is in the United States.
The EU VAT identification number mentioned in Austrian guidance; it is not the only way to establish an American buyer’s business status.
The separate EU report described for qualifying services placed in another EU Member State.
The part of the customer’s business receiving the particular service.

title: A Belgian brand entering America: identify the trademark you own before choosing a filing route
description: Distinguish Benelux and EU protection from an international application and American examination.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Find out what the home record actually protects
paragraphs: Belgium’s Federal Public Service Economy explains that a Benelux trademark covers Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg. There is no separate Belgian trademark in that system. An EU trademark covers the European Union. Neither territorial description should be treated as protection for the American business.

Locate the exact application or registration, current owner and status. Compare the sign and goods/services with what the U.S. operator will actually sell. A shared group name is not a substitute for the owner’s record or a description of the protection needed.

sections.heading: The existing application determines the described route
paragraphs: The official international-route page describes first applying for a Benelux or EU trademark, then using that basic application or registration for an international application through the same office. For the described routes, that office is BOIP or EUIPO.

Keep the basic record, owner and intended countries together. Saying that the business registered in Belgium does not tell the filing team which office of origin applies. It should compare the intended U.S. designation with any alternative national-filing questions before paying for the proposed route.

sections.heading: International registration does not create an automatically valid worldwide mark
paragraphs: The Belgian intellectual-property guidance explains that WIPO sends the application to the designated national offices. Those offices use their normal procedures and may refuse protection. The international registration is therefore a collection of national filings, rather than one unrestricted worldwide trademark.
The U.S. launch still needs its own review of availability, ownership and application basis. This guide performs no live prior-right search, selects no filing basis and approves no application.

sections.heading: Fictional example: the parent owns the brand but the subsidiary signs contracts
paragraphs: A Belgian parent holds a Benelux application. A new American subsidiary will sign customer and franchise agreements. Before paying filing fees, the brand manager records who owns the basic mark, which goods/services it covers, who will use the brand and how American protection is to be pursued.

The subsidiary’s incorporation and a new domain name do not extend the parent’s territorial rights. The team must also decide how the operator’s proposed use fits the owner’s rights. This is an evidence and filing-route exercise, not a finding that the mark is available or that the contemplated licence is complete.

sections.heading: Give the filing adviser an owner-and-mark packet
bullets: Exact owner, sign, basic application/registration number and current status.
The goods/services and territories actually covered and those the U.S. business needs.
The proposed BOIP or EUIPO route, U.S. designation and alternative national-filing questions.
The prior-right search scope, a budget using current official tariffs and a person responsible for examination responses.

practicalOutput: An owner, basic-mark and territorial-coverage file supporting the choice of international or national U.S. filing route.
limitations: This is a Belgian home-country trademark-route guide. It does not clear a mark, establish U.S. registrability, choose a filing basis or file an application.
Current ownership, basic-mark status, service classes, prior rights, national requirements and actual fees must be checked for the intended filing.
Data protection, franchise classification, tax, personnel, treaty eligibility and operating permissions remain independent.
learningSummary: A Belgian business may describe its brand as registered at home without knowing which territory the registration covers. Before licensing the brand to an American operator, identify the actual owner, mark and goods or services, then choose the filing route that fits the existing record.

keyTerms.meaning: A mark covering Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg under the described system.
The existing application or registration on which the described international application relies.
The Benelux Office for Intellectual Property and European Union Intellectual Property Office, the possible offices of origin described here.
The World Intellectual Property Organization, which sends international applications to the designated national offices.
Naming a country or territory in which protection is sought; examination can still follow there.

title: Swiss customer data in a U.S. system: verify the actual recipient’s transfer route
description: Explain Swiss-U.S. certification and alternative safeguards before staff or suppliers receive personal information.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Identify the receiving company, records and purpose
paragraphs: FDPIC explains the Swiss rules for disclosure abroad. The Federal Office of Justice’s current page reproduces the binding adequacy list, whose U.S. entry is qualified by certification under the Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework. It is not an unqualified finding about every American recipient.

Map which entity receives which information and for what purpose. Include service providers, group affiliates and other recipients rather than relying on a parent-company label. This guide has not checked any company’s certification or authorised any particular transfer.

sections.heading: Check the current certification and its actual scope
paragraphs: The official Swiss assessment describes the U.S. Department of Commerce’s public participant list and annual recertification. Withdrawal or failure to recertify can lead to removal. Check the actual recipient’s current Swiss-U.S. participation and the relevant data before relying on that route.

A sales assurance, a parent-company name or certification under another framework does not establish the recorded task. The official 2024 assessment is historical support; the live Justice Office list and FDPIC guidance provide the presently reviewed context.

sections.heading: If that route does not apply, investigate the alternative conditions
paragraphs: For a destination without the relevant adequacy, FDPIC describes safeguards including recognised standard clauses, specific contractual guarantees and approved binding corporate rules. They have different approval or notification requirements. The guidance also identifies Article 17 exceptions.

The controller must consider whether the recipient can comply and whether supplementary technical measures are needed. Signing a generic data agreement does not complete that assessment. This is also only the cross-border part of the problem: lawful processing, security, contracts, employee or sensitive data and onward disclosures need their own fact review.

sections.heading: Fictional example: customer contacts and employee tickets enter a group system
paragraphs: A Zurich parent wants Swiss customer contacts and employee support tickets in a U.S. group system. The data owner lists the provider, American affiliate and any other recipients, then identifies the data, purposes and access paths for each disclosure. Forming the affiliate did not itself establish a transfer route.

For each recipient, the owner checks the applicable certification and scope or documents the alternative safeguard to investigate. The team considers recipient compliance, necessary technical measures and the required information to affected people. It also records who will recheck a recipient, purpose or certification change. These actions turn a general system proposal into a decision about actual data and parties.

sections.heading: Keep the transfer evidence with the system plan
bullets: Source and destination entities, data categories, purposes and access.
Current actual-recipient certification evidence or a documented alternative route.
Recipient-compliance assessment and any necessary supplementary measures.
The processing inventory and information to affected people where required, including countries and guarantees.
An owner to review changes before continuing to rely on the selected route.

practicalOutput: A recipient-by-recipient Swiss transfer record with certification or alternative safeguards, data purposes, technical questions and change ownership.
limitations: This is a Swiss cross-border personal-data transfer guide, not a complete FADP/GDPR compliance program or a specific company certification check.

Swiss-U.S. certification must be current and relevant to the actual recipient and processing. The official 2024 assessment is historical support; the live FOJ list and FDPIC guidance provide the present reviewed context.

Lawful processing, contracts, security, sensitive/employee data, onward disclosures and all other applicable legal requirements need their own fact review. Tax, franchise and staffing permission are separate.
learningSummary: A Swiss company may want its American affiliate or support supplier to use customer and employee records. The cross-border question concerns the actual receiving entity and processing, rather than whether the destination can simply be labelled America or part of the same group.

keyTerms.meaning: Switzerland’s Federal Act on Data Protection, the law discussed in this transfer guide.
The Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner, Switzerland’s data-protection authority.
The relevant official recognition of protection for a destination, subject to the stated scope and conditions.
The certification arrangement relevant to the qualified U.S. entry in the Swiss adequacy list.
The organisation responsible for deciding the relevant purposes and handling of personal data.
The European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation, a separate privacy regime whose applicability and duties need their own assessment.

title: What evidence does an L-1 staff-transfer plan need?
description: Assess the person’s overseas employment, real U.S. duties and any new-office conditions separately from the company link.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Keep company, history and duties as separate questions
paragraphs: The regulation generally calls for one continuous year of qualifying full-time employment abroad within the relevant preceding three-year period, alongside the qualifying organisational relationship and role evidence. A licence agreement, supplier relationship or impressive title does not establish those facts.

Record overseas employment dates and actual duties. Brief lawful U.S. trips can receive specific treatment in the continuous-employment calculation; do not automatically count them as foreign employment. The reviewer needs travel facts as well as a start date.

sections.heading: Explain the person’s work and authority
paragraphs: The managerial definition concerns organisation or function management, appropriate authority and discretion. A first-line supervisor is not a manager solely because of supervision, subject to the professional-employee qualification. Executive and specialised-knowledge roles have their own elements.

Use duties, time allocation, reporting lines and supporting staff to explain the proposed job. A small team’s “general manager” may perform several hands-on tasks, so the title alone does not answer the capacity question. No role qualification is decided by this guide.

sections.heading: A new-office plan needs more than incorporation
paragraphs: For a new-office manager/executive, the regulation requires sufficient physical premises and evidence that the intended operation will support the qualifying position within one year of approval, including the proposed organisation and financial ability. Specialised-knowledge new-office provisions differ.

An owner or major stockholder also has specified temporary-service/assignment-abroad evidence under subsection (l)(3)(vii). These are distinct evidence requirements, not a generic minimum-investment promise. Do not transfer one new-office route’s conditions to another without review.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a technical leader becomes the launch manager
paragraphs: A group proposes moving its technical leader to manage a new U.S. office. The initial plan lists only a title and budget. The operations lead adds foreign employment/travel history, actual technical and management duties, staffing, premises and the intended first-year organisation.

The reviewer can now assess the corporate relationship, qualifying capacity and relevant new-office evidence separately. The owner can remain abroad if the independently assessed staffing plan allows; no founder relocation, petition approval or admission is assumed. Keep forms, fees and processing estimates as separate current checks.

practicalOutput: A person-by-role matrix linking employment/travel history, duties, authority, staff, premises and any additional new-office or owner evidence.
limitations: Scoped regulatory preparation only. No current form, fee, processing time, qualifying role, petition, blanket-route or admission result is established.
learningSummary: A qualifying corporate relationship is only one part of an L-1 plan. The person’s employment history and actual proposed work also matter. Build the evidence around the job and organisation rather than copying a senior title into the application plan.

keyTerms.meaning: The intracompany-transfer category addressed by the cited regulation.
The executive, managerial or specialised-knowledge capacity requiring its own regulatory evidence.
A case with additional requirements for the proposed U.S. operation and role.
The qualifying overseas employment period, whose calculation includes specific rules rather than every trip being counted alike.

title: Does P.L.86-272 protect a service business from state tax?
description: Read the narrow tangible-goods solicitation protection before applying it to services or other taxes.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The protected activity has specific conditions
paragraphs: The federal protection concerns state or local net-income tax where the person’s only in-state activities are the specified solicitation of orders for physical goods. The orders must meet the out-of-state approval/rejection and fulfilment conditions in § 381. Those conditions belong together; this is not protection for every interstate transaction.

It does not say that every out-of-state company, website, royalty recipient or service provider is exempt. The statute also excludes specified state-incorporated corporations and resident/domiciled individuals from that protection. Do not read a short summary as broader than the actual provision.

sections.heading: Do not move a goods rule across to every tax and service
paragraphs: Cleaning, consulting, training and managed IT income cannot simply borrow a tangible-goods solicitation protection by analogy. Even where the provision is relevant to goods, a net-income-tax limit does not settle sales/use, payroll, unemployment or gross-receipts taxes, or corporate qualification.

The statute’s defined independent-contractor treatment is also not a general employment-status ruling. Identify what question a term answers in this provision before carrying it into a different area of law.

sections.heading: Fictional example: remote sales and local service delivery
paragraphs: A foreign service brand has no local office but contracts for work performed at U.S. customer sites. Its team writes “no physical office, no tax” and cites P.L.86-272. That conclusion skips both the nature of the activity and the tax type.

The finance lead records who solicits, approves and performs contracts, what is sold, where people work and which entity receives income. The reviewer then examines current rules for each relevant state and tax. The example does not determine a positive tax connection or return obligation in any particular state.

sections.heading: Build a state-by-tax activity register
paragraphs: Use separate rows for income/franchise, sales/use, payroll and local taxes. Record premises, workers, products/services, contracts, solicitation, approval and fulfilment for each entity.

Add a P.L.86-272 question only where its actual goods/activity conditions may matter. Keep formation and qualification records separate from the tax decision. Current thresholds, sourcing, allocation between states and filing requirements require state-specific research; this federal boundary guide is not a 50-state clearance.

practicalOutput: A state-by-tax activity register showing the actual business facts and where the narrow federal goods-solicitation protection may be relevant.
limitations: No individual state/local tax connection, threshold, taxability, sourcing, apportionment or return outcome is determined. This guide explains the federal statutory boundary only.
learningSummary: A company operating from another state or country may hear that a federal law protects it from state tax. P.L.86-272 has a much narrower subject: specified solicitation of orders for tangible personal property and state net-income tax. A service business needs a separate state-by-tax assessment.

keyTerms.meaning: The federal protection codified in 15 U.S. Code § 381, with defined activities and conditions.
Physical goods, distinct from the service income examples discussed here.
The type of tax addressed by the protection, not every tax a state or locality can impose.
Facts connecting an entity to a jurisdiction for a particular tax, often called nexus.

title: When is a Texas IT service taxable data processing?
description: Classify the actual deliverables and taxable value before calculating an invoice’s tax.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Describe the delivered task rather than the company label
paragraphs: The Comptroller describes entering, storing, manipulating or retrieving a customer’s data as data processing, while merely using a computer to perform a professional service is different. Its examples contrast data work with engineering or bookkeeping judgement and interpretation.

The labels IT, consulting and B 2 B do not classify every invoice line. List the actual deliverables, the customer data involved and the judgement or interpretation supplied. A hosting/storage task and an advisory task may raise different questions even when sold by the same team.

sections.heading: Read the 20% provision as an exemption of value
paragraphs: Texas Tax Code§ 151.0035 defines data processing with exclusions, and§ 151.0101(a)(12) includes it among taxable services. Section 151.351 exempts 20 percent of the value of information services and data processing services. That is not a 20% tax rate or a blanket exemption for IT contracts.

For illustration, if$1,000 is otherwise-taxable qualifying data-processing value, the stated exemption removes$200, leaving$800 before any other applicable adjustments. The actual tax amount still depends on the applicable rates and other facts. The calculation does not determine this contract’s category, sourcing or seller obligations.

sections.heading: Fictional example: data work and advice on one contract
paragraphs: A service business proposes one contract covering data entry, storage and interpretation of results. Renaming the whole invoice consulting does not explain the actual work. Finance separates the deliverables, proposed charges and evidence of customer use.

The Comptroller publication addresses distinct/identifiable nontaxable services, reasonable separate charges and documentation for mixed bundles. It also addresses use inside and outside Texas. The reviewer needs those facts before determining treatment; a new invoice heading is not a substitute for them.

sections.heading: Create a service-line tax schedule
paragraphs: For each deliverable, record the data activity, staff judgement, price evidence, location/use and unresolved classification. Keep the confidential contract and any multistate-use certificates in the authorised accounting process, outside this site.

Separate service classification, exemption/base calculation, seller tax connection or registration, sourcing and final rate. The statutory review is limited to the named Texas sections and the Comptroller guidance is revision 03/2022. Other states and later amendments to their service categories need separate work.

practicalOutput: A Texas service-line schedule showing actual deliverables, price/use evidence, category, partial-exemption question and unresolved collection/calculation tasks.
limitations: No actual contract, mixed-service allocation, exemption, permit, tax connection, sourcing or final tax amount is determined. Other-state taxability is not answered by this Texas example.
learningSummary: A service company may describe everything it sells as IT or consulting, while Texas tax treatment depends on what the customer actually receives. Data processing has a particular statutory definition and exclusions. Separate that service question from whether this seller must register or collect tax.

keyTerms.meaning: The relevant statutory service category, including defined data activities and exclusions; not every professional use of a computer.
The value to which an applicable tax rate is applied after relevant treatment and adjustments.
A provision removing part of qualifying value from tax, rather than supplying a tax rate.
Customer use inside and outside Texas, requiring its own facts and applicable allocation evidence.

title: Does a UK company qualify for U.S.–UK royalty treaty benefits?
description: Check residence, beneficial ownership and the actual limitation-on-benefits route before assuming a reduced rate.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Keep the four entitlement questions distinct
paragraphs: Internal Revenue Service (IRS) guidance identifies relevant residence, beneficial ownership, derivation of income and applicable LOB conditions for reduced treaty withholding. A form or treaty-country mailing address does not replace the underlying entitlement evidence. The payer must consider actual knowledge or reason to know of ineligibility.

Finance should therefore identify the actual recipient and income before placing a treaty rate in the cash model. A change in payee or ownership may change the questions even if the brand and bank account name look familiar.

sections.heading: Read the UK articles and protocol together
paragraphs: Article 4 defines residence. Article 12 addresses royalties with permanent-establishment, special-relationship and conduit conditions. Article 23 contains multiple eligibility routes and limitations. For example, Article 23(2)(f)’s ownership/base-erosion route has both ownership-period and deductible-payment conditions. UK incorporation alone is not that test.

The July 2002 protocol replaces Article 23(7)(d). Do not rely on the unamended equivalent-beneficiary wording in the 2001 PDF. This guide does not resolve a derivative-benefits or post-Brexit question; it identifies the need to use the amended text and applicable route.

sections.heading: Fictional example: the new UK receiving company
paragraphs: A group proposes paying U.S. royalties to a UK company and assumes its registration proves treaty eligibility. The preparer asks instead who owns it during the relevant period, how the income is treated, who beneficially owns it, what deductible payments leave the company and which LOB paragraph is relied on.

Those facts can be assembled without choosing a favourable result. The reviewer checks residence, the royalty article and the selected amended eligibility route separately. The example quotes no treaty rate and does not decide the company’s entitlement.

sections.heading: Produce an article-by-article evidence schedule
paragraphs: For each claimed condition, record the source paragraph, period, evidence custodian and unresolved fact. Link any withholding certificate to the actual recipient and income. Keep the treaty assumption unknown in the cash model until supported.

Tax residence and beneficial ownership are also different from the E-2 enterprise-nationality inquiry. Do not reuse an immigration ownership diagram as a complete treaty file, or copy a UK eligibility path to another country’s treaty.

practicalOutput: A U.S.–UK treaty claim schedule connecting residence, income, ownership, deductible outflows and the precise amended LOB route.
limitations: U.S.–UK illustration only. No rate, treaty entitlement, permanent establishment, conduit, equivalent-beneficiary or post-Brexit result is determined.
learningSummary: A royalty paid to a company with a UK address does not automatically qualify for treaty relief. Incorporation, tax residence and entitlement to the income are different facts. The U.S.–UK treaty also has eligibility conditions designed to limit who can claim its benefits.

keyTerms.meaning: Residence under the actual treaty definition, not simply a registered address.
The relevant entitlement to the income, distinct from merely receiving a payment.
Limitation on benefits: treaty provisions setting conditions for eligibility.
The deductible-payment part of a particular LOB route, which must be assessed alongside its ownership conditions.
A treaty business-presence concept with its own conditions, not every U.S. contact or entity.

title: Nationality and tax residence: first ask whose status matters
description: Keep the owner, foreign parent and U.S. company separate when answering tax, treaty and immigration questions.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Keep the owner and companies on separate rows
paragraphs: The owner, foreign parent and U.S. operating company are different people or entities for these questions. IRS guidance says a non-U.S.-citizen individual’s U.S. tax residence generally turns on the green-card or substantial-presence tests, with specified elections, exceptions and treaty issues. A green card concerns U.S. permanent-resident status; the presence test concerns the relevant U.S. presence facts.

This is different from asking where a company was formed or which ultimate owners have the nationality relevant to an immigration treaty. The article does not count anyone’s days, decide an exception or establish an E-2 immigration entitlement.

sections.heading: A treaty may ask another residence question
paragraphs: For illustration, Article 4 of the U.S.–UK treaty defines residence and has different dual-resident rules for individuals and other persons. For an individual, the sequence considers earlier conditions such as permanent home, centre of vital interests—the closer personal and economic relationships—and habitual abode before nationality appears at a later stage.

That does not make nationality a universal first-step shortcut. Nor can the individual result be copied onto a company. The relevant treaty text and its amendments must be read for the actual person and income; the UK example is not a definition for every other country.

sections.heading: Use this sheet to keep the questions apart
paragraphs: The final column identifies facts or decisions that should not be substituted for the row’s actual test. A treaty payment also needs its income, beneficial-owner and any applicable LOB conditions; a visa question remains separate.

rows: Residence, beneficial owner, LOB and income conditions

sections.heading: Worked example: an owner and a royalty recipient
paragraphs: Fictional example. An owner has one country’s citizenship, lives in the United Kingdom and owns a company that will receive payments from a U.S. operator. A colleague gives the whole group one UK label and uses it both for a treaty assumption and an immigration discussion.

Finance first identifies the actual recipient of the payment and the period. It gathers the company’s own residence and treaty-entitlement facts. Separately, it records the owner’s personal tax-residence facts and any relevant nationality and ownership evidence. Neither the passport nor the owner’s home address has answered all three systems. This example reaches no residence, withholding-rate or immigration conclusion.

sections.heading: A practical record without unnecessary private documents
paragraphs: Prepare one row per person or entity and one period per tax analysis. Identify the question, source, evidence custodian and what remains unknown. The actual identity and tax documents belong with the authorised custodian outside this site. The planning record needs enough information to prevent the wrong person’s status being reused, not a collection of passport or tax-return uploads.

practicalOutput: A person-and-company status sheet separating nationality, personal residence, company residence and payment entitlement.
limitations: No personal tax-residency/day count, treaty tiebreak, entity-residence or immigration approval. UK treaty illustration is not transferable to every country.
learningSummary: An owner’s passport, where the owner lives and where a company is incorporated are different facts. They can be relevant to different rules, but one label cannot answer every question. Start by identifying the person or company whose status is being tested and the period concerned.

keyTerms.meaning: Citizenship relevant to the particular nationality question; it is not automatically the same as tax residence.
An individual’s status under the applicable tax rules, which can differ from an everyday description of where the person lives.
The company’s status under the relevant tax law and treaty definition, separate from its owner’s personal status.
Being treated as resident in both countries under the relevant rules, which can require a treaty’s separate decision process.
The recipient whose entitlement to the income must be examined for the particular treaty-payment claim.
Limitation on benefits: treaty conditions that can restrict which persons obtain benefits even when residence is established.

title: How do brand-quality controls differ from franchise controls?
description: Explain what each requirement protects and whether it also directs how the operator runs the business.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The trademark provisions concern marked goods and services
paragraphs: The trademark definition of a related company concerns the owner’s control over the nature and quality of the marked goods or services (§ 1127). Another provision addresses legitimate related-company use and controlled first use benefiting the registrant/applicant, with a condition against public deception (§ 1055).

These provisions make the actual quality system important. They do not dictate or approve any particular staffing rule, software requirement or inspection programme. A complete licence-validity or abandonment opinion would also require the applicable law and cases beyond this statutory distinction.

sections.heading: The franchise inquiry asks a different question
paragraphs: The FTC framework separately examines brand association, significant operating control or assistance, and required payment. Calling a provision trademark protection does not decide its practical effect.

Separate artwork approval from requirements about scheduling, staffing, sales methods or mandatory systems. A control can have mixed purposes. Record both rather than forcing it into one category to obtain a preferred legal label. The May 2008 FTC guide provides explanatory context, read with the current rule.

sections.heading: Fictional example: logo approval and a scheduling system
paragraphs: A brand requires approval of vehicle logos and also dictates job acceptance, staff allocation and customer scheduling through mandatory software. The operations lead explains the quality outcome protected by each requirement and how defects are checked and corrected.

The reviewer can then examine trademark use and the wider operating relationship separately. Deleting every check to avoid one test may leave an unanswered trademark question; adding detailed management controls may create franchise questions. The example does not declare either document valid or the arrangement a franchise.

sections.heading: Keep both preparation records
paragraphs: One file identifies the owner, authorised user, quality standards, inspections and corrections for marked goods/services. The second explains the complete business relationship for federal and independent state franchise analysis.

For every control, name the quality attribute, business effect, person checking it and correction process. Route the unanswered questions to the relevant reviewer. This practical table helps reveal mixed purposes; it is not a statutory safe harbour or a complete survey of uncontrolled-licensing case law.

practicalOutput: A control-purpose matrix and two linked records: trademark quality/use evidence and the broader operating-relationship factsheet.
limitations: Statutory distinction only. No complete licence-validity, abandonment, trademark case-law or franchise-coverage conclusion is made.
learningSummary: A brand owner wants a reliable service under its name, but detailed operating rules can also raise franchise questions. Those two concerns should be assessed together without treating them as the same legal test. Document what a control does rather than assuming its heading decides the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A name, logo or other sign identifying the commercial source of goods or services.
For the cited trademark definition, a person whose marked goods/services are subject to the owner’s nature-and-quality control.
A requirement directing the method of running the business, assessed separately under the franchise framework.
An internal table explaining each standard’s quality purpose, business effect and checking/correction process.

title: Why is a sanctions name search only the first step?
description: Match the actual party, trace relevant ownership and assess the proposed transaction under the right restrictions.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: A similarity score is not transaction clearance
paragraphs: Commerce says apparent CSL matches need additional due diligence and confirmation against the official source list. A fuzzy-name score measures similarity, not the probability that a deal is lawful.

Record names, aliases, appropriate identifiers, addresses, source list and search date. Explain why an apparent match is or is not the actual party. Do not treat all lists alike: identify the restriction associated with the particular source and person before deciding the consequence.

sections.heading: Ownership can affect an entity not separately listed
paragraphs: OFAC FAQ 401 explains direct/indirect ownership and aggregation under the 50 Percent Rule. Its examples show why simply multiplying every percentage can mislead. If a blocked person owns 50% of Entity A, A is blocked; A’s 50% ownership of Entity B can in turn make B blocked.

A search for Entity B’s name alone could miss that result. Trace the chain and apply the actual ownership rule rather than assuming a missing name means no restriction. Equally, do not replace the prescribed analysis with an informal control test.

sections.heading: Control and other transaction restrictions remain separate
paragraphs: FAQ 398 says control without 50% aggregate ownership is not automatic blocking under this ownership rule, but warns about other designation/blocking criteria and dealings involving a blocked representative. Below 50% is therefore not universal permission.

Party screening also does not settle goods or technology, destination, end-use, country-programme or authorisation requirements. A country connection is not always a blanket ban, just as a clean name result is not a complete export decision.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a prospective distribution partner
paragraphs: A brand considers a distributor whose name produces no apparent match. The team records the result but also obtains the relevant ownership chain and the proposed goods, destination and use. It assigns any unresolved source-list and transaction questions before payment, access or shipment depends on clearance.

The screening register should identify the reviewer and source-specific result, then be revisited when parties, ownership, goods or restrictions change. This site performs no live search and does not certify a partner as clean.

practicalOutput: A screening-and-transaction register documenting identity matches, ownership, source-specific restrictions, actual transaction facts and remaining questions.
limitations: No live designation result, country/programme decision, export classification, licence or transaction authorisation is provided.
learningSummary: A screening tool can return a possible name match without deciding whether the person is the same party or whether the transaction is permitted. An unlisted business can also be affected through ownership rules. Keep identity, ownership and the transaction as separate questions.

keyTerms.meaning: The Consolidated Screening List, combining specified Commerce, State and Treasury lists as an aid.
The Office of Foreign Assets Control, which administers the ownership rule discussed here.
A person subject to the relevant blocking treatment; not every list entry has identical restrictions.
The OFAC ownership rule reaching entities 50% or more owned in aggregate by blocked persons, including relevant indirect ownership.

title: Can a brand require common prices across its network?
description: Distinguish brand/operator restrictions from coordination among competing businesses and review the actual policy.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Understand what Leegin actually decided
paragraphs: In Leegin Creative Leather Products v. PSKS,551 U.S. 877(2007), the Supreme Court majority overruled the prior Dr. Miles federal per-se treatment of vertical minimum resale-price agreements and required rule-of-reason analysis. The Court reversed and remanded—sent the case back for further proceedings.

That outcome is not a finding that every policy, or the particular arrangement, was lawful. The cited record supplies the 2007 majority’s standard and disposition, not an independently checked later merits outcome. Current FTC guidance also explains that state-law treatment can differ.

sections.heading: Map who competes and who makes the decision
paragraphs: FTC guidance distinguishes manufacturer/dealer restrictions, unilateral policy decisions and competitor coordination. A network can contain several relationships, especially where the brand also operates units.

Record whether operators coordinate or collectively pressure the brand. Calling an arrangement vertical does not settle horizontal effects. State and international minimum-price rules may also differ from the federal framework. MAP, MFN, territory and customer restrictions require their own actual terms to be examined.

sections.heading: Fictional example: operators ask for a common price
paragraphs: Several independent service operators ask the brand to establish a common network price. The brand also has its own operating unit. Rather than assuming the request is an ordinary brand standard, the team preserves who proposed it, the communications, competitive relationships and intended enforcement.

The reviewer can then distinguish suggested from required prices, unilateral decisions from agreement, and the claimed service/quality purpose from effects on competition. The example clears no price policy or customer allocation and makes no finding about the fictional parties.

sections.heading: Prepare the policy before announcing it
paragraphs: Keep the proposed rule, discounts, advertising support, territories, reserved customers and methods used to induce compliance. Preserve communications and evidence supporting any claimed service investment.

Build a policy/party/effects file with separate federal, state and international questions. The standard of review tells the reviewer what must be examined; it is not a badge of legality to place beside a standard price list.

practicalOutput: A policy/party/effects file explaining the pricing or allocation restriction, communications, competitive relationships and jurisdiction-specific questions.
limitations: No antitrust clearance, later Leegin outcome or complete case-law survey is supplied. No MAP, MFN, territory, customer or collective-pricing arrangement is approved.
learningSummary: A brand may want consistent prices, territories or customer allocations across independent operators. The competition-law analysis depends on who agrees, who competes and how the policy works. A federal case changing the standard of review did not make every network pricing policy lawful.

keyTerms.meaning: A restriction between businesses at different supply levels, such as a supplier and dealer; the actual relationships matter.
Coordination between competitors, distinct from a supplier imposing its own policy.
A legal approach treating a defined category as unlawful without the fuller analysis discussed here.
An assessment of the actual arrangement and competitive context, not automatic approval.
Minimum advertised price terms, whose actual reach needs separate examination.
Most-favoured-nation terms linking one party’s treatment to others; their conditions also require review.

title: State payroll accounts: a guide to withholding and unemployment registration
description: Understand the two account decisions, prepare the employer and worker facts, and use the 50-state and D.C. tables without treating gaps as exemptions.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Why one payroll dashboard can require several government accounts
paragraphs: Your overseas business may hire a U.S. manager and a few technicians before it opens a permanent office. Paying them involves more than arranging a bank transfer or giving their details to a payroll company. The legal employer needs to identify the relevant government accounts, the payments each account covers and the dates on which reporting begins. This comparison addresses state employer-account preparation across all 50 states and the District of Columbia.

There are two different account decisions throughout the tables. Wage-income withholding concerns income tax deducted from employee pay and sent to the relevant tax agency. Unemployment insurance, abbreviated UI, concerns the state system supporting eligible unemployed workers and the employer’s related reporting and contribution duties. The names differ: some entries use “reemployment” or “unemployment compensation.” A conclusion about personal income tax does not answer the UI question.

A federal Employer Identification Number, or EIN, identifies the business for federal tax purposes; FEIN means the same federal identifier. Forming a company, obtaining its EIN, creating a payroll-provider login and opening a state payroll account are separate actions. Some states use combined applications or common account numbers, while others use separate agencies. A shared application does not make the legal tests identical.

The entries retain some agency terminology: a “workstream” means a separate set of related tasks, and “nexus” means a connection that may matter for a tax duty. Neither word establishes the duty by itself. Agency source links identify the relevant authority; an official portal’s account labels and form codes are identifiers to check against that agency’s instructions.

Use each table’s labels carefully. “Conditional” means the stated route or requirement must be matched to your actual facts. “Unresolved” means a substantive question or access problem remains. “Not researched” means this review has not established the answer. “Not applicable” closes only the specific personal wage-income withholding question described in that row. None of these labels is permission to ignore other payroll duties.

sections.heading: Prepare the facts before asking someone to register the employer
paragraphs: Give the payroll lead a worker-by-worker schedule: legal employer, proposed employee or contractor status, home state, each physical work location, service start date, first pay date and expected travel or remote-work pattern. The state where you formed the company, the employee’s residence and the state where services are performed can be different. The entries below identify which facts the named agencies request; they do not supply a universal allocation rule for multi-state work.

For an owner or company officer receiving pay, add the business’s legal form, relevant tax election and remuneration. An LLC is a limited liability company; an S corporation reference concerns a particular tax treatment. The name of the legal form alone does not answer every state’s treatment of a paid owner. For an acquisition, add the seller, assets or workforce acquired, transaction date and predecessor accounts. Do not assume that the buyer may keep reporting under the seller’s number.

Ask the payroll provider to return the actual agency account confirmations, liability notices, tax types activated, effective periods and first filing dates. Liability means that the relevant law applies to the employer under the stated facts; a notice may identify when that duty begins. Creating a portal user or saving a draft is different from submitting an application, receiving an account number or filing an accepted return. Where an agent handles payroll, use the agency’s authorisation process rather than assuming the provider’s login proves the employer is registered.

Plan the timing from the particular state entry. Some agencies require action before withholding or paying wages, while others direct registration after an actual wage payment or liability event. An open account may require zero returns even when there is no tax to pay. That is why registering speculatively, or treating every state as if it had the same first-hire deadline, can create problems.
bullets: Ask who is authorised to create the employer account and how the payroll agent receives access.
Resolve allocation between states, any resident-state withholding and relevant local withholding before setting deductions.
Revisit the accounts when the EIN, legal entity, ownership, location or employee work pattern changes.
Keep federal employment taxes, wage-and-hour rules, work authorisation, workers’ compensation, paid leave and local taxes on a separate list of checks.

sections.heading: Alabama
paragraphs: Give payroll the actual work-state and residence list. Keep the ALDOR account confirmation separate from the SR-2/UI determination rather than assuming one registration creates both.

rows: ALDOR directs employers with employees working in Alabama to obtain a withholding account through My Alabama Taxes. Its FAQ separately addresses Alabama residents working elsewhere, including withholding for the work state.
The Labor eGov Employer Registration service accepts Form SR-2 to determine SUI liability and obtain an account; a portal login is not itself a liability determination.

bullets: The eGov page contains older dated notices; only its identified registration function was relied on. UI thresholds, classification exceptions and current rates were not verified.

sections.heading: Alaska
paragraphs: For a foreign service company sending a crew to Alaska, identify who hires, directs and benefits from the work before choosing the reporting entity. Multi-state work needs a localization review rather than an automatic headquarters-state account.

rows: An Alaska personal-income-tax withholding conclusion was not established in this review. Do not infer the absence of other employee deductions or payroll obligations.

TaxWeb registers new businesses; the agency handbook requires UI accounts for workers hired and working in Alaska and says workers brought from elsewhere may also need reporting. The registration requests entity type and first wage date.

bullets: The retrieved handbook says last updated April 2024. This review uses its account/localization instructions, not annual contribution rates or a complete current exemption determination.

sections.heading: Arizona
paragraphs: A company that already holds an Arizona withholding account still needs the UI application route. Track each agency's determination instead of treating the joint form as a single approval.

rows: DES identifies the Joint Tax Application JT-1/UC-001 and an existing-withholding-account route, but the separate DOR withholding-obligations page returned HTTP 403. Withholding liability and sourcing remain unresolved.

Submit JT-1/UC-001 through DOR; DES uses it to decide UI liability and separately issues a determination stating the coverage start date, rate and eight-digit account number. The EIN is required for processing.

bullets: This records the DES process and separate review, not a conclusion that every Arizona business owes UI or withholding. DOR substantive withholding access remains blocked.

sections.heading: Arkansas
paragraphs: Do not substitute a federal UI threshold for Arkansas's stated ten-day ordinary-employer test. Assemble paid-work days, first wage date, ownership and acquisition facts before the Tax 21 session, which the agency says has no save option.

rows: The 2026 DFA instructions require withholding registration through AR-1R and identify ATAP online registration. They distinguish work in Arkansas from work outside it and allocate nonresident partly in-state services to Arkansas workdays.

The Reemployment agency uses Tax 21 and describes ordinary employer status after one or more workers perform services on ten or more days in a calendar year, plus acquisition, domestic, agricultural and voluntary-coverage categories.

bullets: Special employer categories have separate tests; the ten-day statement is not a universal threshold. The withholding PDF's employment-verification statements were not relied upon for federal I-9 rules.

sections.heading: California
paragraphs: Enroll the portal user, verify the email within EDD's stated 24-hour window, then submit the separate New Employer application. Preserve the eight-digit payroll account number; user enrollment alone does not create it.

rows: EDD registers employer payroll tax accounts through e-Services for Business and supplies distinct commercial, household, agricultural, nonprofit and other forms. Select the correct account category rather than treating incorporation as payroll enrollment.

EDD Step 1 requires a business that hires employees and pays more than $100 in wages in a calendar quarter to register within 15 days. Household employment has a separate $750 cash-wage threshold; use the appropriate account category.

bullets: Annual tax rates, wage bases, excluded employment, disability and paid-leave contributions require their own current review. Registration does not resolve worker classification.

sections.heading: Colorado
paragraphs: A foreign or other out-of-state employer should follow the CR 0100 branch rather than assuming the in-state portal route applies. Assign a separate owner to resolve CDLE unemployment registration.

rows: DOR requires a withholding-agent account when Colorado withholding is required. Its instructions distinguish in-state businesses using MyBizColorado or CR 0100 from out-of-state businesses using CR 0100; the account has no fee or renewal requirement.
The attempted CDLE registration page returned HTTP 403. The UI account procedure, liability thresholds and multi-state allocation were not substantively verified.

bullets: This establishes a conditional withholding-account process, not the underlying wage sourcing test, UI clearance or freedom from local occupational/payroll taxes.

sections.heading: Connecticut
paragraphs: Record both legal entity type and tax election before deciding whether an owner-manager's remuneration belongs in UI reports. An S corporation's federal income-tax treatment does not by itself exempt its paid officer's services from Connecticut UI.

rows: DRS links withholding to maintaining an office or transacting business in Connecticut and federal employer status, regardless of payroll department location. Register through myconneCT or add withholding to an existing DRS account.

DOL requires online ReEmployCT registration for employers of one or more people and separately describes liability thresholds. It expressly distinguishes sole proprietors, partners, paid corporate officers and LLC members according to relevant tax filing treatment.

bullets: The agency's LLC/officer discussion is Connecticut-specific. Family, nonprofit, domestic and other special coverage conditions still need fact-specific review.

sections.heading: Delaware
paragraphs: Map the employee's residence and actual work location before choosing full employer registration or withholding-agent-only treatment. Keep UC-1 submission and the resulting liability decision with the payroll file.

rows: One Stop distinguishes an employer conducting business in Delaware from an out-of-state business that may register as a withholding agent only for a Delaware resident as a courtesy. Do not turn that optional resident-service route into a universal duty.

One Stop directs businesses hiring one or more employees in Delaware to file UC-1 to determine unemployment liability and identifies withholding and workers' compensation as separate employer workstreams.

bullets: Only agency routing and the residence/work distinction were relied upon; older form names and broad withholding language on One Stop were not treated as complete current computation guidance.

sections.heading: Florida
paragraphs: Classify a service business as general, domestic, agricultural or another category before applying a threshold. Preserve the DR-1 determination; the guide treats corporate officers and LLC members differently according to the stated facts and tax classification.

rows: DOR expressly states Florida does not impose personal income tax. This closes only the state personal wage-income withholding branch; reemployment tax, corporate tax, sales tax and other payroll/business obligations remain separate.

DOR's reemployment guide requires DR-1 to determine liability; quarterly reports alone do not register an employer. It states general $1,500 quarterly wages, one employee in 20 weeks, or federal unemployment-tax liability tests, with separate special-employer categories.

bullets: The reemployment guide is revised March 2025; its annual rates were not relied on. The separate DOR tax guide supports the table’s narrow personal-income-tax statement. Worker classification and a complete current exclusion review remain outside this record.

sections.heading: Georgia
paragraphs: Put the first Georgia payroll date on the launch calendar and assign DOL-1A immediately afterwards. Keep payroll withholding and nonresident owner/distribution withholding as separate finance questions.

rows: DOR identifies employee-wage withholding, a separate registration-for-withholding-number route and Form G-4. Its page also covers other payment types, so a payroll number is not a determination of every nonresident-payment duty.

GDOL directs employing units with people performing services in Georgia to submit DOL-1A immediately after the first Georgia payroll. The FAQ separately states general liability and domestic/agricultural tests.

bullets: The DOR page contains a general rate description and the UI FAQ contains older wage-base text; neither was relied on as current rates or wage bases.

sections.heading: Hawaii
paragraphs: A Hawaii-based company sending staff outside the state cannot assume all wage withholding disappears. For UI, establish the owner's authorized account first and delegate the payroll provider through agency permissions.

rows: DOTAX states withholding applies to services in Hawaii and specified services outside it linked to the regular workplace or paying office. Obtain the WH account using BB-1 or add it in Hawaii Tax Online; the account has no opening fee.

The UI agency generally links tax to employees working in Hawaii and requires business owners to create the employer profile, after which they may authorize staff or service companies. Nonprofit, family-corporation and successor elections have separate conditions.

bullets: The withholding page contains inconsistent older return-form guidance; only its account and sourcing sections support this entry. Special UI elections are applications, not automatic exclusions.

sections.heading: Idaho
paragraphs: If a sole proprietorship becomes an LLC or a foreign buyer acquires operations, check the new-account branch. Using the predecessor's withholding voucher does not establish the buyer's own account.

rows: Obtain the EIN first, then use Idaho Business Registration. The Tax Commission says a withholding account is not transferable and requires a new account on business acquisition, a new EIN or a change of entity.

The Tax Commission's IBR guide routes businesses with employees to income-tax withholding and employee-related permits from Labor and the Industrial Commission. Prepare expected employee count, first paycheck and hire dates.

bullets: The separate UI handbook URL returned 404; IBR routing is verified, but Labor's substantive UI liability thresholds and localization are unresolved.

sections.heading: Illinois
paragraphs: Include a startup date and any purchase/reorganization in the payroll brief. The same portal can serve both agencies, but withholding registration and UI succession are different determinations.

rows: IDOR requires registration when Illinois withholding is mandatory or voluntarily undertaken and asks when Illinois payroll begins. MyTax Illinois/REG-1 handles registration; household employment has separate guidance.

IDES directs newly created employing units to register within 30 days of startup through MyTax Illinois or the liability form. A merger, acquisition or entity change has a separate succession/update workstream.

bullets: The 30-day statement is the agency's employing-unit registration rule, not a conclusion about every entity's tax liability. No current rate or full reciprocal-state analysis was performed.

sections.heading: Indiana
paragraphs: Record the actual Indiana work location and county before payroll setup. Creating an ESS user and obtaining the employer SUTA account are separate steps; use the agent route for a payroll provider.

rows: DOR directs employee businesses to collect state and county wage withholding, obtain an EIN and register through INBiz. It expressly points to county-specific rates rather than one statewide payroll setting.
DWD's Uplink ESS registration requires FEIN, legal name, NAICS, Indiana work location, first payroll date and responsible-party details; the SUTA number follows completed and approved registration.

bullets: This records account inputs and the existence of county withholding. It does not select an employee's county rate, settle reciprocity or verify every UI coverage exception.

sections.heading: Iowa
paragraphs: Treat a remote Iowa hire by a foreign or other out-of-state employer as a distinct registration event. Use a properly authorized agent account, not shared employer credentials, and confirm the applicable multi-state allocation before reporting.

rows: IDR links withholding to an office or business in Iowa, federal withholding and services performed in Iowa; obtain FEIN before Iowa registration. Residence and multi-state services still require the applicable sourcing review.

IWD says register through myIowaUI within 30 days of first Iowa wages or acquisition; out-of-state employers must register as soon as Iowa wages are paid. It separately discusses base-of-operations and direction/control for multi-state workers.

bullets: The agency page has a 2026 note changing out-of-state wage credits alongside older text; no wage-credit amount is asserted here. Account routing is not full employment-law coverage.

sections.heading: Kansas
paragraphs: Do not put a Kansas client's payroll under the reporting agent's own tax number. Identify resident versus nonresident workers and distinguish the employer's wage account from any owner-payment withholding.

rows: KDOR's KW-100 directs covered employers/payers to register through its Customer Service Center and separately addresses Kansas-resident and Kansas-work wages. It distinguishes wage withholding from nonresident-owner accounts and reporting-agent accounts.
The KDOL employer-services page returned HTTP 403; the current UI account route, timing and liability test were not substantively verified.

bullets: KW-100 displays revision 24.08. Its registration and account distinctions were reviewed, not current rates or a comprehensive 2026 wage-sourcing exception inventory.

sections.heading: Kentucky
paragraphs: Budget access to MyTaxes before payroll rather than assuming a paper-payment route. Assign a separate UI registration check and a local occupational-tax review for the employee's actual locality.

rows: DOR identifies resident/nonresident wage withholding subject to exemptions and directs registration, filing and payment through MyTaxes. Its 2026 instructions require electronic filing/payment for all employer filing frequencies.

The official employer page routes liable employers to an Employer Reserve Account, including acquisitions. The January 2026 KUIP FAQ says an account number and report filing are available immediately after completed registration.

bullets: The attempted UI-1 link returned non-substantive content; the separate official employer page and January 2026 KUIP FAQ were read. Liability thresholds, local occupational taxes and current rates remain separate.

sections.heading: Louisiana
paragraphs: Time account activation to the actual withholding start rather than opening it speculatively. Separately determine whether LAWATS needs a new employer account or access to an existing account, and preserve the agency's resulting status.

rows: LDR requires a withholding account before filing/remitting, but specifically warns not to register until Louisiana wage withholding begins. LaTAP registers a new business or adds an account; Secretary of State registration and EIN do not create it.

LWC's LAWATS login instructions require an existing seven-digit Employer Account Number and FEIN; a business without the EAN must apply for the unemployment tax account first. The owner then grants a third-party administrator access.

bullets: The LAWATS login guide is dated April 11, 2024. It distinguishes portal access from the tax account but does not establish current UI liability thresholds or sourcing exemptions.

sections.heading: Maine
paragraphs: A New Hampshire employer with a Maine resident should document work and business-location facts, not infer Maine withholding solely from residence or solely from headquarters. Preserve the distinction between mandatory and courtesy withholding.

rows: MRS's April 2026 FAQ routes new withholding accounts through the Maine Tax Portal and separately tests an out-of-state employer's Maine office/business, taxable payments and federal withholding. Courtesy withholding can differ from mandatory withholding.

The official ReEmployME guide distinguishes registration of a business without an EAN from creating access to an existing account. It states general and separate nonprofit/agricultural coverage tests and says a future date cannot be used to set up an account.

bullets: Official www1.maine.gov mirrors supplied the MRS FAQ and ReEmployME system guide after the main host blocked access. No annual rate, complete UI exclusion list or full remote-work sourcing determination is supplied.

sections.heading: Maryland
paragraphs: Record remuneration to a paid officer and the actual employing entity before labeling a small company 'owner only.' After BEACON, obtain a separate Comptroller withholding answer rather than treating UI enrollment as all tax registration.

rows: The 2026 Comptroller guide requires CRA registration and a Central Registration Number, warns not to wait until withholding is due, and says an acquirer must not use the seller's number. The September 2026 CRA guide routes applications through Maryland Tax Connect.

Labor requires an employer UI account through BEACON, distinguishes covered from excluded work and expressly includes paid corporate officers in covered employment. Other tax registration and UI are separate.

bullets: Withholding and UI registration are separate from Maryland FAMLI, local withholding computations, worker exclusions and full wage sourcing. No annual rate or paid-leave date is asserted.

sections.heading: Massachusetts
paragraphs: A short Massachusetts assignment by an out-of-state company deserves its own UI review; do not automatically substitute a familiar $1,500 threshold from another category or state. Distinguish proprietor income from wages to an employee.

rows: DOR's August 2026 guide distinguishes resident and nonresident wages and directs employers to register before filing/payment through MassTaxConnect. A sole proprietor is generally not an employee solely for paying their own personal tax.

DUA lists general contribution tests and distinct domestic/agricultural categories; it specifically states an out-of-state employer test of $200 gross Massachusetts wages in a quarter. Its account route is Unemployment Services for Employers.

bullets: The $200 statement is the agency's out-of-state-employer category, not a universal tax-free allowance or a withholding threshold. No annual rates or full sourcing exceptions are supplied.

sections.heading: Michigan
paragraphs: Confirm the current MiUI workflow rather than reusing an old payroll-provider checklist. Keep the employer's own access and authorize the third party through the agency route; a provider's login is not the employer's registration evidence.

rows: Treasury's MTO business-tax eRegistration process and separate user/business-account linkage were read, but that general page does not establish withholding liability, sourcing or account-selection criteria. Those remain unresolved.

UIA's current help center says MiUI is live for all tax/benefit functions and employers should hold their own MiUI account even when using a third-party administrator. It separately routes business registration and account authorization.

bullets: The reviewed Treasury page covers business registration generally; withholding liability and sourcing require a separate substantive tax analysis. No broad Michigan tax clearance is implied.

sections.heading: Minnesota
paragraphs: Minnesota's withholding and UI account timing differ: prepare withholding before deductions, but do not preregister UI before covered wages are actually paid. Retain both numbers and resolve owner/officer coverage before selecting wage records.

rows: DOR's new-employer guide requires a Minnesota ID and withholding account before tax is withheld. It distinguishes that number from DEED's UI account used for state unemployment reporting.

The UI handbook says register after covered wages have actually been paid and before the first required quarterly wage-detail report is due. It asks entity type, owner/officer interests, Minnesota work dates and acquisition facts, with special categories treated separately.

bullets: Covered employment, owner/officer elections, nonprofit and other special categories still require their own tests. This is not a Paid Leave registration or full employment-law determination.

sections.heading: Mississippi
paragraphs: A recruitment-platform registration does not activate unemployment reporting. For an acquisition, tell DOR the ownership/entity facts and retain the correct acquiring-employer account before the first post-acquisition payroll.

rows: DOR requires a withholding account for employers subject to Mississippi withholding, with online application through TAP. Its instructions require acquisition/entity changes to be assessed rather than using the predecessor's addressed return.

MDES separates employment-service registration from the New Business unemployment-tax registration, and separately offers online access for an already assigned account. An employer needing both service categories must register for both.

bullets: This does not establish UI liability thresholds or all resident/nonresident sourcing rules. No annual withholding/UI rate is supplied.

sections.heading: Missouri
paragraphs: Keep the legal entity filing, DOR withholding number and UI liability outcome as three records. A foreign company temporarily sending a team should also investigate the transient-employer category before assuming ordinary registration is sufficient.

rows: DOR's 2026 guide directs employers paying wages to employees working in Missouri to register online or using Form 2643. The permanent withholding number is not transferable; transient-employer requirements are a separate category.

Labor's new-employer guide distinguishes Secretary of State formation from DOR tax registration and directs the employer to a separate UI liability review. New liable employers receive an industrial classification for UI.
